newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Morgan Grenfell says may own 57 pct Sintercast.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Grenfell says may own 57 pct Sintercast.

text.p: Morgan Grenfell on Friday said three of its investment funds currently under investigation may own up to 57 percent of A-shares in Swedish development company Sintercast and up to 98 percent of its B-shares.

Morgan Grenfell Asset Management Ltd (MGAM) said it became aware of the holdings, which could represent 58 percent of voting rights in the company, during its enquiries into the funds managed by two of its subsidiaries.

The group holdings mean direct and indirect holdings of funds managed by companies in the group involving MGAM and subsidiaries and the shares which may now be held indirectly by Deutsche Bank AG but may previously have been held by funds managed by MGAM companies.
"MGAM is in discussion concerning the results of its enquiries and their implications, if any, with relevant regulators," MGAM said in a statement.
"MGAM will make a further announcement in relation to this holding once more information is known."

MGAM said Deutsche Bank AG has agreed with the trustees of the investment funds in question that it will not dispose of its indirect holdings in shares in Sintercast for at least one year or before the funds have disposed of their holdings.
The funds under investigation are Morgan Grenfell's European Growth Trust, Europa Fund and European Capital Growth Fund.
Sintercast is a Swedish listed company, a highly speculative stock, that has developed a system for casting car engine blocks.
Heavy trading in Sintercast in recent months, largely by Fiba Nordic Securities, had driven the share price to a high of 550 crowns this summer, brokers said.
On Thursday Sintercast shares plummeted 40 crowns by the close to end at 270 crowns in heavy trade.
